outcome: proportion of pregnant patients undergoing cervical length screening
method of cervical length screening used by physicians (e.g., transvaginal ultrasound)
proportion of physicians treating pregnant patients with a short cervix
treatment modalities used by physicians for short cervix (e.g., progestogen type)
physicians' preferred treatment for short cervix if reimbursement was not a concern
cohort: 500 physicians treating pregnant patients with a short cervix in the United States were surveyed.
finding: While US physicians largely adhere to guidelines for cervical length screening using transvaginal ultrasound, there is a divergence in preferred treatment for short cervix, with many opting for synthetic progestin despite national recommendations for vaginal natural progesterone.
